newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges rise on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges rise on short covering.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges began the week on the upside, gaining some $1 with buying interest seen from market players covering short positions, traders said.
High sulphur barges initially traded at $86.25 to $86.75 fob ARA, or a little higher than Friday's close, before moving up to $87.25 by mid-day.
A trading house was said to be the seller at the first set of figures, while an independent oil trade sold at the highest figures, traders said.
Some traders said there was short cover buying in the market but others said that sellers were just charging a little more for prompt material.

Low sulphur barges were inactive but notionally assessed a little lower, at $94/$96 for buyers and sellers respectively. Traders said lack of demand from Germany may be one of the reasons behind the inactivity seen in that market recently.
High sulphur cargoes were talked at the two means +$1 for 11 Engler material, which translates into two means minus $2 for lower quality cracked material, traders said.
"There's the famous $3 missing on Russian cargoes. These people think that these are the values of Russian material but that's why there have been deals recently," one trader said.
Russian high sulphur straight run continues to be scarce on the E-4 and M-40 front, with only one cargo of the later loading soon and none seen of the former.
M-100, of which five or six cargoes will load soon, was on offer at a steady two means plus $2/$2.50 while M-40 was valued at two means plus $5/$6.
